---
title: "Conversion Guide"
---

This guide defines the repeatable workflow for converting older source
material into the Quarto site.

## Rmd to Qmd

1. Copy the source `.Rmd` into a temporary working branch or scratch
   folder.
2. Preserve code chunks, equations, and figures, but rewrite the prose
   into the lecture page pattern.
3. Replace institution-specific labels, term dates, and assignment
   references with neutral wording.
4. Move long code demonstrations into lab pages when they interrupt the
   lecture narrative.
5. Render the page and fix warnings before linking it from the roadmap.

## LaTeX Slides to Notes

Slide decks are useful for topic order, figures, and concise examples,
but the website should read like teaching notes. Convert slides into
sections rather than embedding slide-by-slide prose.

For each deck:

- extract section titles,
- identify equations and figures worth keeping,
- rewrite bullets as paragraphs,
- cite or recreate figures only when permissions are clear,
- place slide-specific details in maintainer notes.

## PDF References

External PDFs should be treated as references unless licensing allows
redistribution. Use them to improve explanations and reading lists, not
as copied course content.

## Suggested Page Template

```markdown
---
title: "NN: Lecture Title"
---

Opening paragraph.

## Learning Objectives

- Objective 1.
- Objective 2.

## Core Ideas

Concepts, notation, and equations.

## Worked Example

Data, model, result, interpretation.

## Lab Hook

How the lab reinforces the lecture.

## Source Notes

Maintainer-only local paths and provenance.

## Build Status

What remains before this page is student-ready.
```

## Render Check

Run:

```powershell
quarto render
```

The build should pass before new pages are treated as part of the
published lecture set.
